2|import { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
3|import { join } from 'node:path';
4|import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
5|
6|// ⛔ EVERY TEST'S TEMP DIRECTORY LIVES INSIDE ONE PER-RUN ROOT THAT IS DELETED WHOLESALE.
7|//
8|// Measured 2026-09-02: 379,380 leaked directories in %TEMP%, 328,427 of them ours, ~26 GB,
9|// accumulating since 2026-05-31 at roughly 2,000–4,000 per full suite run. Dozens of test files
10|// call `mkdtempSync` and each relied on its own `afterAll`; the ones that forgot were invisible
11|// because nothing checked. The volume eventually hit 100% and the suite died with ENOSPC.
12|//
13|// Node's `os.tmpdir()` reads TEMP/TMP (Windows) or TMPDIR (POSIX) at CALL time, so redirecting them
14|// here relocates every `mkdtempSync(join(os.tmpdir(), …))` in every worker — and anything a spawned
15|// child writes to its own temp dir, clangd included — without touching a single test file.
16|//
17|// ⇒ Computed at config-evaluation time because the value has to reach BOTH the worker `env` below
18|// and the globalSetup teardown, which runs in this process.
19|const RUN_TMP = join(tmpdir(), `apg-vitest-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`);
20|mkdirSync(RUN_TMP, { recursive: true });
21|process.env.APG_TEST_TMP_ROOT = RUN_TMP;
22|
23|export default defineConfig({
24|  test: {
25|    // Deletes RUN_TMP after the run, and prunes roots abandoned by a crashed one.
26|    globalSetup: ['./tests/helpers/temp-root.global.js'],
27|    include: ['tests/**/*.test.js'],
28|    testTimeout: 30000,
29|    hookTimeout: 30000,
30|    // REAL-SERVER TESTS MUST NOT RACE EACH OTHER.
31|    //
32|    // tests/integration/code-intel/* each spawn a real language server (clangd,
33|    // tsserver, pyright). Run concurrently they compete for CPU, and a cross-TU
34|    // reference query can be issued before the server has finished parsing its
35|    // warmup files — so a legitimately-absent caller fails the assertion. It
36|    // reproduced twice under full-suite load and passed every time in isolation.
37|    //
38|    // Two earlier fixes were the wrong shape: waiting on INDEX readiness (the index
39|    // being ready is not the same as this file being parsed), then waiting on the
40|    // per-file parse signal. The second was right on its own terms and made the
41|    // product more honest — batchWarmup no longer sleeps a fixed duration — but no
42|    // wait can conjure CPU that four concurrent language servers are already using.
43|    //
44|    // The remaining cause is contention, so the fix is scheduling, not another
45|    // timeout. A flaky test is worse than a slow one: it teaches the reader to
46|    // re-run rather than to look, which is exactly how a real regression gets waved
47|    // through.
48|    fileParallelism: false,
49|    // ⚠ PINNED, NOT INHERITED. `tests/unit/freshness/relative-reporoot.test.js` calls
50|    // process.chdir() to prove a RELATIVE repoRoot resolves the same as an absolute one —
51|    // and process.chdir() throws inside vitest's `threads` pool ("not supported in
52|    // workers"). It passes here only because the CURRENT default happens to be `forks`.
53|    //
54|    // ★ review, hermes session hit exactly that restriction running an isolated archive,
55|    // and reported it among failures they could not attribute. The suite was relying on a
56|    // DEFAULT to satisfy a hard requirement — and a default is not a decision, it is
57|    // whatever the tool picked this version. It has already moved once (vitest 2 changed
58|    // from threads to forks), so this would have broken on an upgrade with a failure that
59|    // looks like a test bug rather than a config assumption.
60|    //
61|    // ⇒ Stated explicitly so the requirement travels with the repo rather than with my
62|    // installed version.
63|    pool: 'forks',
64|    // ★★ THE WHOLE SUITE RUNS SEALED. In production a packet route that emits a candidate
65|    // list without consulting the shared disclosure renderer gets a loud caveat appended —
66|    // degrading a user's answer is better than crashing their call. Under test it THROWS,
67|    // so any test that so much as touches such a route fails hard instead of quietly
68|    // recording the caveat as expected output.
69|    //
70|    // ⇒ This is what makes the guarantee route-sensitive rather than function-sensitive.
71|    // review, hermes session killed the source inventory by adding a disclosure-less branch
72|    // INSIDE graphPacket — which the inventory passed, because that 396-line function calls
73|    // the renderer elsewhere. Nothing pattern-matched over source can attribute a header to
74|    // the path that produced it. Executing it can.
75|    // ⛔ AND THE SUITE'S VERDICT MUST NOT DEPEND ON MACHINE LOAD.
76|    //
77|    // graph_packet bounds a symbol→feature lookup at 2000ms in production. That lookup's own
78|    // measured cost is 601ms on a 3958-node repo and 4316ms on a 12126-node one, so on a busy
79|    // machine it crosses the line, packet takes its TIMEOUT branch, and every test asserting on
80|    // CONTENT fails. Measured on one unchanged tree in a single session: 680s / 2120s / 2693s with
81|    // 0 / 2 / 10 failures — failures scaling with duration, all budget-shaped.
82|    //
83|    // That destroys the signal the "full suite green before push" gate exists to give: a real
84|    // regression becomes indistinguishable from contention, and three separate investigations in
85|    // that session ended in "it was load".
86|    //
87|    // ⛔ AND THE VALUE IS BOUNDED ON BOTH SIDES — "loses no coverage" was WRONG at 30000ms.
88|    //
89|    // Two classes of test pull in opposite directions:
90|    //   CONTENT tests need the lookup to COMPLETE, so the budget must exceed a real lookup.
91|    //   TIMEOUT tests (packet-timeout-not-absence) MOCK A HANG FOREVER to prove a timeout is not
92|    //     reported as an absence, so they fire at exactly the budget — and at 30000ms that blew
93|    //     their own 20s test limit, turning four real assertions into test timeouts. Those tests DO
94|    //     assert on latency behaviour, which is the coverage I claimed did not exist.
95|    //
96|    // 8000ms satisfies both: above any realistic fixture lookup (measured 601ms on a 3958-node
97|    // repo, and these fixtures are far smaller) even under the 4x load seen today, and below the
98|    // 20000ms test timeout so a mocked hang still fires inside it.
99|    //

Fixed in mcp/stdio/query/verbs/callers.js:52.

Cause: SQL fetched at most 101 unscoped edges, then sliced to 100 before applying the directory filter. Those rows could all come from the other directory, yielding a false NO CALLERS. SQL also lacked ordering, so later LSP_VERIFIED edges could disappear before ranking.

Changes:
  Directory filtering now happens in SQL before LIMIT.
  Caller queries prioritize LSP_VERIFIED edges before the cap.
  Recursive traversal still crosses out-of-scope intermediate nodes.
  Fixed the equivalent scope-after-cap bug in graph_callees, including virtual overrides.

Added tests/unit/query/caller-callee-fetch-scope.test.js with 17 tests covering the reproduction, heuristic matches, direct and recursive queries, verified-edge priority, and literal path-prefix semantics.
